findings.title: Race condition: check-then-update allows over-redemption
findings.explanation: The plain SELECT takes no row lock, and the later UPDATE no longer guards on `redemptions < max_redemptions`. Under READ COMMITTED (the default), two concurrent requests can both read redemptions = max-1, both pass the check, and both increment, so the coupon is redeemed more times than allowed. The original single atomic UPDATE prevented this. Fix: use `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, or better keep the atomic conditional UPDATE (with its WHERE guards) and only run the diagnostic SELECT when rowCount is 0 to work out the reason.

findings.title: Unconditional UPDATE drops the guard on expiry and max redemptions
findings.explanation: `UPDATE coupons SET redemptions = redemptions + 1 WHERE code = $1` has no protection if state changes between the SELECT and the UPDATE (expiry, concurrent redemptions). Even with a lock, defence in depth suggests keeping the original conditions and checking rowCount.

findings.title: Expiry is checked against the app clock instead of the DB clock
findings.explanation: The original used the database `now()`. `expires_at <= new Date()` uses the app server clock, which may be skewed, and depends on the pg driver parsing timestamps into Date (a timestamp without time zone could be parsed incorrectly). Compare in SQL (e.g. select `expires_at <= now() AS expired`) for consistency.

findings.title: Distinct errors enable coupon code enumeration and change the API contract
findings.explanation: Separating `coupon_not_found` from the other errors lets an authenticated caller probe which codes exist, and there is no visible rate limiting on this endpoint. The `coupon_unavailable` response also disappears, which may break existing clients. Consider rate limiting, and confirm the clients and docs are updated. The distinct statuses might also be better as 404 for not found and 410/422 for the others, rather than a blanket 409.

findings.title: No tests for the new error paths
findings.explanation: Add tests for not_found, expired, used_up, and a concurrent-redemption test that verifies the max is never exceeded. Also, `'error' in result` works, but a discriminated union with an explicit `ok` field would be clearer.

## Return specific errors when a coupon can't be redeemed

Support keeps asking why a coupon "didn't work". This splits the single UPDATE into a lookup plus explicit checks, so the API can say whether the code is unknown, expired, or used up. Still runs in one transaction.
